title: Max-intensity ladder: 5x3min uphill treadmill to 15%

steps.target: 15% or max holdable, 180-188 bpm, empty it

coachNotes:
EXECUTION: ladder, 5x3min at 12-15% incline with 3min walking at 5% between. Rep1 12% / 168-174, rep2 13% / 172-178, rep3 14% / 175-182, rep4 14% / 175-182, rep5 15% or max holdable / 180-188 and empty it. 15min warmup rising to 3%, non-negotiable. 12min flat cooldown. Reference: 27 Aug treadmill hit 188 max at RPE 8 and was absorbed cleanly - that is the ceiling, not a target to beat.
GYM: none.
FUEL: 1 gel 20min before, water during.
STOP RULE: no symptoms during, after, or next day. Lateral knee pain on any rep ends the session, do not test the next one. Calf or Achilles tightness also ends it: at 15% and 185 bpm the posterior chain is the exposed tissue, not the band, and a calf strain 11 days out ends the race as completely as the ITB would.
WHY THE LADDER AND WHY IT IS ALLOWED: steep uphill is the lowest-ITB-risk way to go hard - no eccentric phase, knee held outside the 20-30 degree compression band - so if max intensity goes anywhere in this block it goes here. The ladder exists because the documented pattern is starting hard sessions conservatively and finishing under prescription; it puts the maximum where it will actually be reached. This is the last time the intensity dial gets touched before 12 September.
